title: Agastya evidence graph
scope: Curated first-pass seed, not an exhaustive concordance. Translation checks and scholarly reports only; original-language philological review is pending.
identity_policy: The five Agastya facets are source-local dossiers. Their labels organize traditions; neither one historical individual nor five separate people is asserted.

status_definitions.translation_checked: Claim inspected in an accessible primary-text translation; does not certify historical truth.
status_definitions.editorial_attribution: Speaker or hymn-author identification depends on editorial/traditional interpretation.
status_definitions.scholarly_report: Scholarship reports the tradition; underlying primary passage has not been checked in this pass.
status_definitions.identity_hypothesis: Proposed identification; exclude from explicit named-attestation counts.

chronology.label: Ṛgvedic textual horizon
chronology.range: Latter half of the second millennium BCE
chronology.note: Broad corpus horizon from Jamison–Brereton; not a dated birth, death, or individual hymn. Oral composition complicates finer dating.

chronology.label: Later Vedic reception
chronology.range: After the hymn tradition; absolute range not assigned here
chronology.note: Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.5.5 already treats a hymn as Agastya’s; a date for this particular layer remains to be sourced.

chronology.label: Contemporary of Rāma and Daśaratha
chronology.range: Rāma’s exile; friendship with the preceding king
chronology.note: Internal synchronism only. Does not independently supply a BCE year.

chronology.label: Tretā-yuga linkage
chronology.note: Bhāgavata 9.10.51 puts Rāma’s reign in Tretā. Linking Agastya to it combines two texts; it is not an explicit birth date for Agastya.

chronology.label: Rāmāyaṇa formative period · Nagy synthesis
chronology.note: Broad scholarly model of epic formation; individual Agastya passages may have different histories. Earlier oral material and later growth are not excluded.

chronology.label: Past deeds in Yudhiṣṭhira’s narrative present
chronology.range: Earlier than Lomaśa’s account to the Pāṇḍavas
chronology.note: The pilgrimage story establishes earlier deeds, not a meeting or a dated death. In §104 Agastya has not returned from the south as of the narrator’s present.

chronology.label: Nahuṣa’s curse
chronology.note: The duration belongs to Nahuṣa’s serpent curse. It is not Agastya’s age and is not used as a calendar anchor.

chronology.label: Mahābhārata formative period · Nagy synthesis
chronology.note: Broad corpus formation, not the date of the war or the date of Agastya.

chronology.label: Bhāgavata · Holdrege’s dating
chronology.note: Numeric endpoints are visualization approximations to the source’s century wording. Applies to text, not narrated persons.

chronology.label: Bhāgavata · Ray’s older proposal
chronology.note: Historical alternative in the dating literature; not represented as equal to a current consensus or as Agastya’s lifetime.

chronology.label: Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar commentary witness
chronology.note: Dates this witness to the disciple tradition, not the origin of every Tamil Agastya tradition and not the life of Tolkāppiyar or Agastya.

chronology.label: Indus cultural-memory hypothesis · Mahadevan
chronology.range: Post-Indus migration interpretation; no individual lifespan
chronology.note: A modern interpretation of legends and undeciphered signs; no independently read Agastya inscription or secure absolute date is established.

open_work: Align all epic passages to the Sanskrit and the critical apparatus; preserve current edition-specific numbering.
Audit the full Ṛgveda 1.165–191 attribution block and its named persons/places against an Anukramaṇī and a modern translation.

Check Aitareya Āraṇyaka 1.2.2, Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 10.11, Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā 2.1, Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 5.16, Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 2.7.11, Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 21.14; citations are leads, not verified graph edges.
Read Tamil primary witnesses: Paripāṭal, Cilappatikāram, Maṇimēkalai, Vīracōḻiyam, Iraiyaṉār Akapporuḷ commentary, and Tolkāppiyam commentaries; source each date and variant.
Expand Purāṇic coverage beyond Bhāgavata and distinguish unrelated works called Agastyasaṃhitā.
Add Agastya/Canopus as a separate celestial entity after checking astronomical texts; do not infer a human lifespan from stellar visibility.
Investigate whether the epic Trasadasyu is identifiable with Vedic attestations, without automatic name merging.
Review manuscript witnesses, inscriptions, regional geography, Buddhist Akitti traditions, and Southeast Asian reception.
